chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered that nothing should be removed from the clothes of the slanderer except the robe.

key_terms.الْقَاذِفِ: The slanderer, one who accuses another of zina without proof

ai.seo_question: What specific clothing is removed from a slanderer during the hadd penalty according to the Prophet's order?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, tracing back to Imam al-Sadiq, clarifies a specific procedural detail in the application of the hadd penalty for slander (qathf), emphasizing the preservation of the accused's dignity by removing only the outer cloak (rida'). This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing justice with mercy, ensuring that the punishment does not degrade the individual beyond the prescribed legal limits.
